stories.body: Devastating floods and landslides triggered by an apparent glacier collapse have killed at least 633 people across Nepal and Tibet, while nearly 3,000 people remain missing. Nepal has suspended some search and rescue operations because of worsening weather and says it lacks the specialised equipment needed for the emergency. Authorities are trying to identify a growing number of bodies, while damage to roads, hydropower facilities and remote mountain communities is complicating relief efforts. Nepal estimates reconstruction could cost $4 billion to $5 billion, and foreign governments are working to account for citizens stranded or missing in affected areas.
stories.headline: Nepal-Tibet floods kill more than 600 as thousands remain missing

stories.body: At least 27 people were killed and 42 injured after a Russian drone strike hit a warehouse in the Bucha district west of Kyiv, setting off a major fire and explosions that damaged nearby homes. Ukrainian officials said more than 380 people were evacuated and have opened an investigation into whether ammunition or other explosive materials were stored improperly at the site near residential areas. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the strike was followed by a detonation and said those responsible for any safety failures would face consequences. The attack came amid intensified long-range strikes by both Russia and Ukraine.
stories.headline: Russian strike on warehouse near Kyiv kills at least 27 people

stories.body: President Donald Trump says the United States has reached an agreement with Venezuela giving it majority control over more than 65 billion barrels of proven oil reserves. Trump said the arrangement, negotiated with interim President Delcy Rodríguez through a private-sector partnership, would increase US oil supply and lower gasoline prices, though the agreement's terms, participating companies and legal structure have not been released. Rodríguez said the deal would develop 17 oil fields and bring more than $100 billion in investment. The proposal could face legal and constitutional challenges in Venezuela, where the state traditionally controls core oil-industry activities.
stories.headline: Trump announces deal giving the US majority control of Venezuelan oil reserves

stories.body: Icelanders are voting on whether to resume negotiations to join the European Union, 13 years after accession talks were suspended. Polls suggest a very close result, with the latest survey putting opponents narrowly ahead. A yes vote would only restart negotiations, not commit Iceland to membership: any eventual accession deal would require approval in a second referendum, in parliament and by EU member states. Supporters cite economic stability, lower inflation and security concerns, while opponents argue that EU membership could weaken Iceland's sovereignty and control over its important fishing grounds.
stories.headline: Iceland votes in close referendum on reopening EU membership talks

stories.body: Niger's military government says it is gradually regaining control after mutinous soldiers held personnel hostage at a military base beside Niamey's airport. Sustained gunfire and explosions were reported near the airport, Base 101 and the presidential palace, while soldiers blocked access to key sites and national television went off air. Officials said security forces had launched search operations and that some attackers had been neutralised, though details could not immediately be independently verified. The unrest underscores continuing insecurity in Niger, which has been ruled by a military government since the 2023 coup.
stories.headline: Niger's military government says it is regaining control after unrest in Niamey

stories.body: Iran's leaders have acknowledged the severe economic effects of six months of war with the United States, saying sanctions and a US naval blockade have reduced imports and exports by nearly 35 percent. President Masoud Pezeshkian said the government must address inflation, jobs and dependence on the dollar, while annual inflation reached 66 percent last month. Tehran nevertheless says it will pursue diplomacy and defense together, maintaining its position on the Strait of Hormuz while seeking talks on reopening shipping. Iranian officials also stressed national unity and resistance to US pressure.
stories.headline: Iranian leaders acknowledge war's economic toll while pledging diplomacy and defense

stories.body: Minnesota is seeking the extradition from Texas of an Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer charged with shooting an immigrant, setting up a dispute over a process that is normally routine between states. The case has become politically charged and could test how state leaders handle extradition requests involving federal immigration enforcement officers.
stories.headline: Minnesota and Texas clash over extradition of ICE officer charged in shooting

stories.body: The Trump administration has asked the Supreme Court to allow the military to discharge transgender service members. The justices could decide whether to hear the case during the term that begins in October, potentially putting the administration's policy toward transgender troops before the court.
stories.headline: Trump asks Supreme Court to permit discharge of transgender troops

stories.body: An autopsy report obtained by the Associated Press says Tyrin Johnson, a 20-year-old man fatally shot by Tennessee National Guard members in Memphis, was struck by a bullet that entered through the right side of his back and exited through his upper chest. The finding conflicts with authorities' previous account that Johnson turned toward Guard members with a gun and was shot in the chest while running from them. The Guard members were assigned to a federal anti-crime task force in Memphis, where the task force was involved in four fatal shootings between May and July.
stories.headline: Autopsy says man killed by Tennessee National Guard in Memphis was shot in the back

stories.body: Investors and policymakers are awaiting a new report on job openings and a closely watched August employment report after July figures showed an unexpected stall in the US labor market. Weakening employment, persistent inflation and falling consumer confidence present a difficult balance for the Federal Reserve, which has kept interest rates steady. Higher oil prices linked to the US war with Iran and the effects of trade disputes have added to pressure on household budgets, sharpening concerns for the Trump administration ahead of the midterm elections.
stories.headline: Jobs data put US economy and Trump under pressure before midterms

stories.body: Spain has asked the European Commission for support from Frontex, Europol and the EU asylum agency to help identify, process and potentially return migrants who remain in Ceuta after a mass arrival at the end of July. The government wants Frontex assistance extended at nearby ports and has requested satellite surveillance of the border with Morocco, while seeking additional support for asylum interviews and investigations into migrant-smuggling networks. About 5,000 migrants remain in the city, where the crisis has intensified debate over Spain's role in protecting the EU's external border.
stories.headline: Spain seeks EU support to process migrants amid Ceuta crisis

stories.body: Spain's health minister says 3,800 migrants who arrived in Ceuta in late July are now in temporary accommodation and that the remaining people still without housing could be rehoused within two to three weeks. The effort follows rising tensions in the city, including attacks with stones on deployed military personnel, the burning of makeshift migrant shelters and competing demonstrations. Officials say housing is necessary before identification, family reunification, health assessments and asylum processing can proceed, while the government has pledged that any returns will comply with human-rights law.
stories.headline: Ceuta works to rehouse thousands of migrants as tensions and violence persist

stories.body: Nepal's tourism board says two of three Spanish nationals reported missing after the catastrophic floods near the Chinese border have been located alive and are in contact with authorities, though they have not yet been rescued from cut-off areas. Nepal says hundreds of foreign tourists remain unaccounted for as rescue teams work across areas damaged by the flood. Spain's diplomatic services in India, Nepal and China continue coordinating with local authorities while monitoring the situation.
stories.headline: Spain locates two nationals reported missing after Nepal floods

stories.body: Barcelona Metro's L1 has resumed service between Florida and Plaça de Sants after a six-week closure for infrastructure work. TMB renewed around 2.1 kilometres of track, upgraded drainage, signalling and track equipment, and modernised parts of the Santa Eulàlia workshop in an investment of €11.5 million. The work included replacing ballasted track with concrete-supported track on part of the route, a change expected to reduce vibrations, improve reliability and make maintenance easier. A replacement bus service operated during the closure.
stories.headline: Barcelona Metro's L1 resumes full service after six weeks of works

stories.body: Residents of three buildings in Barcelona's Sant Gervasi neighborhood evacuated after a sinkhole linked to L9 construction will probably be unable to return home until early 2027. Authorities say the ground must be fully stabilised and the tunnel-boring machine moved away from beneath the buildings before returns can be authorised. Eighteen homes and seven businesses are affected in the three properties, while residents of a fourth building are expected to return by early October. The July sinkhole forced evacuations from eight buildings and is expected to delay completion of the L9 tunnel by several months.
stories.headline: Residents of three buildings evacuated after L9 sinkhole may not return until 2027

stories.body: Barcelona is on track to record its hottest summer, with unusually dry conditions compounding the heat. The Fabra Observatory recorded only about 32 litres of rain per square metre between June 1 and August 28, well below the city's typical summer total of roughly 100 litres. The dry summer follows a wetter-than-normal winter and spring, and water reserves remain close to 80 percent, but longer-range forecasts suggest limited chances of significant rainfall in the first weeks of September.
stories.headline: Barcelona's summer is on course to be its hottest on record
